title: The message text of MSG-P7-009 and of the chain warning MSG-P7-012 is named in the sources but never written
source: FSD P7 Decision center and log v3 A2.2.4.3 (AC-EXC-P7-002-01, AC-EXC-P7-002-05), A2.3.4.3 and the validation rules of A2.1; TSD P7 Decision center and log v2 T-A.2 API-P7-006; Legacy RWB-E1-018 section 14
section: Section 5 Exception paths X1 to X3 and X5; section 7 AC2, AC3 and AC7; section 14 Validation and messages
description: Three of the refusals this story answers carry a message ID whose text no source writes. MSG-P7-009 is named for a rule ID with no rule version, for a model refused in a state that is not in force and for a decision code outside the list, and the criteria only require it to name the field. The chain warning MSG-P7-012 is named only in the target stories of this service; the legacy key carries no warning for a broken chain at all, because in the monolith the chain was checked by a nightly job and not on a read. A message catalogue entry is needed before the answer text can be fixed, and section 14 cannot invent a sentence.
evidence: FSD P7 AC-EXC-P7-002-01 reads 'it is refused with message MSG-P7-009 naming ruleVersion' and AC-EXC-P7-002-05 reads 'it is refused with message MSG-P7-009 naming decisionCode'; neither gives the sentence. The TSD P7 T-A.2 error lists give only the HTTP codes. Legacy RWB-E1-018 section 14 lists MSG-P1-001, MSG-P3-025, MSG-P3-027, MSG-P7-003, MSG-P4-002 and MSG-P4-003 with their texts and carries no MSG-P7-009 and no MSG-P7-012; MSG-P7-003 is the only P7 message the legacy key writes out in full.
proposed: Write both sentences in the message catalogue before wave 1: MSG-P7-009 as one sentence naming the field and the case reference, and MSG-P7-012 as one warning naming the chain position, and add both rows to the API specification of this service.

title: The case-creation filter of the ledger read and the field list of its answer are not specified in any source
source: TSD P7 Decision center and log v2 T-A.1 API-P7-006 and T-A.2 (query: caseId, decision, ruleId, approver, from, to, page, size); FSD P7 A2.2 and A2.3; Legacy RWB-E1-018 section 12
section: Section 1 Story; section 4 Flow step 7; section 7 AC1 and AC5; section 12.1 Contract
description: The ledger read this story extends exists in the TSD with eight query parameters, and none of them selects a final call, so the case-creation profile cannot ask for the creation entry alone. The legacy key read the case and its accounts by case ID through two case endpoints, which are rwb-case's in the target, so the only read a P7 slice can offer is a filter on the ledger. No source fixes the parameter name, whether the answer is a page or one entry, or whether the profile fields are the entry fields of the TSD or a narrower projection. The answer field set of this story is therefore a default and not a copied value.
evidence: TSD P7 T-A.2 API-P7-006 gives 'Query: caseId, decision, ruleId, approver, from, to, page, size' and 'Response: DecisionLogPage'; API-P7-007 reads one entry by ID. TSD P7 T3.1 gives the twenty-three fields of decision_log_entry and no projection. Legacy RWB-E1-018 section 12 declares the job output and two case read paths under the monolith base, and its acceptance criteria read the case and its account links rather than the ledger.
proposed: Add finalCall to the query parameters of API-P7-006 in the API specification and fix the answer of the creation filter as a page of entries with the thirteen fields this story names, so the audit query of RWB-P7-E2005-APP and this profile read share one shape.

title: TSD P7 still models decision_log_entry.case_id as a uuid with a relationship to recovery_case and gives the row no business-date column
source: TSD P7 Decision center and log v2 T3.1 DF-DEC-002 and T3.3; Architecture v5 slide 8 and slide 13; Template and Rules v1 section R5.5 DP-01; Legacy RWB-E1-018 section 11
section: Section 4 Flow step 6; section 8 BR11; section 11 Data; section 12.7 Contract
description: The data dictionary keeps a cardinality row from decision_log_entry to recovery_case, which in a per-service schema can only hold across a schema boundary. The target forbids a service reading another service's tables and forbids cross-schema keys, so the reference has to be an indexed business key with no foreign key. The same table also has no column for the business date the legacy record carries, so the date travels inside the inputs reference rather than in a column. Both facts change the storage of a required value, and the legacy key names neither.
evidence: TSD P7 T3.1 DF-DEC-002 reads 'case_id | CROSS_REF | uuid | No'; TSD P7 T3.3 reads 'decision_log_entry | case_id | recovery_case | Many to 0 or 1'. Architecture v5 slide 8 states 19 Recovery schemas with one login each and no service reading another's tables; DP-01 of Template and Rules R5.5 reads 'Owner's schema rwb_<name>; never read another service's tables'. Legacy RWB-E1-018 BR11 requires the business key with no foreign key, and its flow step 11 carries the ALS business date on the record.
proposed: Restate DF-DEC-002 as an indexed business key with no foreign key and drop the recovery_case row of T3.3, and state in T3.1 that the ALS business date is carried inside inputs_ref, so the ledger holds no case attribute and no cross-schema key.

title: The literal rule ID of the ENTER rule of package ENTRY is named in no source
source: Legacy RWB-E1-018 flow step 7, BR1 and the acceptance criteria AC1 and AC2; FSD P7 A2.3; the registry stories of this service; TSD P7 T3.1 DF-DEC-004
section: Section 3 Preconditions; section 7 AC1; section 11 Data; section 16 TC-E1-018-01
description: The profile requires the ENTER rule ID on every case-creation record, and the legacy key names the rule only as 'the ENTER rule ID of package ENTRY'. Two rule IDs of the same key are written out, EXCL-004 and EXCL-006, both belonging to package EXCLUSION, and no source gives the identifier of the rule that admits a case. The entry must therefore carry the rule ID that the published record carried, and a fixture cannot assert a value that no source holds.
evidence: Legacy RWB-E1-018 flow step 7 reads 'the ENTER rule ID and package version are carried to the decision log' and never names the rule; AC2 gives rule ID 'EXCL-004' and AC6 gives 'EXCL-006', both of package EXCLUSION. FSD P7 A2.3 defines the entry fields and names no rule. TSD P7 T3.1 DF-DEC-004 gives the column and no value.
proposed: Have the package ENTRY workbook name its admitting rule in the rule-row catalogue and copy that identifier into the registry fixture of this story, so the contract test asserts a value from a source rather than a placeholder.

title: A secondary slice carries no build dependency while its fourteen DP rows add eight platform contracts and four published contracts
source: Template and Rules v1 section R5.4, R5.5 and R5.7 rule 8; the WP line for RWB-P7-E1018-APP; RWB-P7-E1008-APP; RWB-P7-E1073-APP
section: Section 3 Preconditions; section 12 Contract; section 13 Solution plan
description: The WP fixes Depends on (build) as empty and Contract dependencies as RWB-P3-E1018-CON only. The fourteen DP rows of this key add eight platform contracts and four published contracts, and the rows this story reads are written by two wave-1 stories of the same service. No source says which of them block the start of a secondary slice, and the metadata rows may not be changed.
evidence: The WP line for RWB-P7-E1018-APP reads H: [] and C: [RWB-P3-E1018-CON]; R5.4 makes H the only blocking class and R5.7 rule 8 makes Ready to start Day 1 when the only H dependencies are contracts; RWB-P7-E1008-APP and RWB-P7-E1073-APP are wave-1 stories of the same service whose rows and fixtures this story reads.
proposed: Record in the build sequence that a secondary slice builds against the platform contracts and the fakes of section 12.8 and reads the same service's wave-1 tables in its own schema, so the lane stays inside the depth limit of R5.7 rule 5 and no dependency row moves.

title: The per-service database login name of rwb-decision is named in no source
source: Architecture v5 service table and slide 8; TSD P7 Decision center and log v2 T1; Template and Rules v1 section R4; the Ownership Map
section: Section 1 Story; section 3 Preconditions; section 13 Configuration and reference data
description: Every service carries one login of its own and no document names it. The story therefore refers to the rwb-decision login and never to the shared monolith login, and the name has to be set in the platform DB story before the deployment.
evidence: TSD P7 T1 describes one service with one repository and one front end and names no login; Architecture v5 slide 8 states one ACE PostgreSQL server with 19 Recovery schemas, one login and connection pool each, and no login name; the Ownership Map assigns the schema and the tables, not the credentials.
proposed: Fix the login name in RWB-PLT-DB and in the secret store, with the migration role and the application role kept apart, and reference it from every P7 story.
